slides.title: GoalWise
slides.subtitle: One focused planning loop for one savings goal
bullets: User question: am I on pace, and what can I safely spend this week?
Success claim: deterministic backend outputs make the answer explainable and defensible.
slides.notes: 0:45. Open with the user problem, then state the engineering claim: GoalWise is intentionally narrow so the calculation and demo can be defended.

slides.title: A narrow MVP beats a broad budget app
slides.subtitle: GoalWise deliberately optimizes around one active goal and manual assumptions.
bullets: One active savings goal
Manual income and planned expense inputs
Backend-owned dashboard values
Canonical planning CSV import as a structured edge input
Deferred: bank sync, raw transactions, multi-goal support, background scheduling
slides.notes: 0:55. Make the scope explicit. This prevents the audience from evaluating the project as a full Mint-style budget app.

slides.title: The financial core is isolated and auditable
slides.subtitle: React renders values; FastAPI validates, calculates, persists, and explains.
bullets: React + Vite frontend over versioned /api/v1 JSON
FastAPI service layer owns validation and ownership checks
Pure pace engine returns deterministic pace-v1 results
SQLAlchemy/Alembic persist PostgreSQL-compatible records
Snapshots and dashboard read model expose committed results
slides.notes: 1:00. Walk left to right: browser, API, services, pace engine, snapshots, dashboard. Emphasize the frontend does not copy the formula.

slides.title: Deterministic pace-v1, no AI in the money path
slides.subtitle: Financial outputs must be reproducible for identical inputs.
bullets: Claim: safe-to-spend, shortfall, and pace status come from a deterministic engine.
Evidence: pace-engine contract and golden tests target stable results.
Rejected alternative: AI-generated calculations would be harder to verify.
Risk: simple formulas may feel less adaptive than personalized advice.
Mitigation: keep explanations separate from the calculation authority.
slides.notes: 1:00. This is the strongest architecture decision. Use claim, evidence, alternative, risk, mitigation, falsifier.

slides.title: Immutable snapshots make results defensible
slides.subtitle: Every committed calculation keeps normalized inputs and versioned results.
bullets: Claim: calculations are stored as immutable snapshots after input changes.
Evidence: snapshot schema and repository tests protect stored results.
Rejected alternative: recompute-only history would hide what the user saw.
Risk: snapshots add storage and schema discipline.
Mitigation: store normalized aggregate inputs, not raw transaction descriptions.
slides.notes: 0:55. Tie this to auditability: the system can explain what it showed at the time without mutating old records.

slides.title: Security boundaries match the hosted demo
slides.subtitle: Auth, CSRF, ownership checks, and Railway config are treated as product behavior.
bullets: HTTP-only server-side sessions with hashed opaque tokens
CSRF required for authenticated unsafe methods
Cross-user private resource access returns 404
Railway uses secure cookies, explicit origin allowlists, and PostgreSQL
Failure case: unauthorized or cross-user access fails without leaking private data
slides.notes: 0:55. Explain that these are not decorative backend details; they define whether a hosted financial demo is trustworthy.

slides.title: AI is useful at the edge, not in control
slides.subtitle: The runtime AI layer explains committed snapshots and can fail without blocking planning.
bullets: Allowed: explanation prose from minimized aggregate snapshot fields
Allowed: development support for tests, diagrams, review, and slides
Blocked: AI calculating, overriding, or recommending official money outputs
Review gate: schema validation, snapshot matching, and human claim approval
slides.notes: 0:55. Be precise about the boundary. The course can ask about AI use, so separate runtime behavior from development assistance.

slides.title: Tests target the risky contracts
slides.subtitle: The evidence is strongest where correctness, privacy, and deployment could fail.
bullets: Pace-engine golden scenarios for calculation behavior
API tests for auth, dashboard, financial inputs, CSV import, and AI explanations
Cross-user access tests for ownership isolation
Migration smoke checks for PostgreSQL-compatible persistence
Frontend lint, TypeScript, Vite build, and visual capture scripts
slides.notes: 1:00. Say what testing proves and one honest gap if asked: it does not prove production load behavior or every future financial scenario.

slides.title: Now we will prove the core path
slides.subtitle: The demo is scoped to value, safe failure, and engineering evidence.
bullets: Value path: create or load a plan and view weekly safe-to-spend
Failure path: invalid or unauthorized access fails safely
Evidence path: show snapshot/test/deployment proof
Transition: browser app first, terminal evidence second
slides.notes: 0:25. Keep this slide short. It is the handoff into the live app, not another architecture explanation.
